dublinCore.description: Read-only timeline of ten landmark synthesizers from the 1920 Theremin to the 1987 Roland D-50, color coded as Early Innovations, Analog Revolution and Digital Era.
relation: Chapter 15: Signal Processing Applications and AI Integration

learningObjectives: Sequence the ten milestones in chronological order, from the 1920 Theremin through the 1987 Roland D-50
Classify each instrument as Early Innovations, Analog Revolution or Digital Era and state the technology that defines each category
Explain why the Minimoog Model D (1970) is described as portable and integrated, in contrast with the modular systems of 1963 and 1964
Compare the Yamaha DX7 (FM synthesis), Kurzweil K250 (stored samples) and Roland D-50 (samples plus synthesized waveforms) as three different digital approaches
Identify the Prophet-5 as the first fully programmable polyphonic synthesizer with patch memory
prerequisites: Know that a synthesizer is an electronic instrument that generates audio signals
Familiarity with the terms oscillator, filter and waveform

misconceptions.misconception: Each year on the timeline is the day the instrument was invented
misconceptions.correction: A year marks a milestone, not a single invention date; design, demonstration and first sales can fall in different years
misconceptions.evidence: The Buchla card says 1963, when Don Buchla began designing his first modules, but the assembled system was sold commercially from 1966; the Prophet-5 was designed in 1977 and shipped in 1978

misconceptions.misconception: The K250 was the first sampling synthesizer, and all digital synthesizers work alike
misconceptions.correction: The Fairlight CMI (1979) was an earlier instrument with an embedded sampler, and the DX7 computes sounds by FM synthesis instead of playing back recordings
misconceptions.evidence: The three Digital Era cards describe three different methods: FM synthesis (DX7), stored samples (K250) and samples plus synthesized waveforms (D-50)

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A vertical timeline of ten synthesizer milestones from 1920 to 1987. Each card gives the year, the instrument name and a one-line description, and is color coded as Early Innovations (blue), Analog Revolution (purple) or Digital Era (pink). The timeline has no controls; scroll to read it.

visualElements.description: Legend: three colored squares naming the categories Early Innovations, Analog Revolution and Digital Era
Ten cards in year order, each with the year on the left and a colored card showing the instrument name and a one-line description

instructionalStrategies: Compare three digital synthesis methods using the card text and references
extensions: Add the Fairlight CMI (1979) to the timeline and decide which category it belongs to
